claims.source: Comparison of the two books' published scenarios
claims.text: The divergence between the 1991 and 1994 Randle-Schmitt crash scenarios is evidence that the Roswell witness pool was being over-fitted: the same authors, working the same case three years apart, produced materially different impact sites and timelines. Reasoning: scenario instability of that magnitude across a single research team indicates witness supply exceeding witness quality.

conflicts: Kevin Randle publicly broke with Schmitt in the mid-1990s over Schmitt's misrepresentation of his own occupation and credentials.

label: Donald R. Schmitt
narrative: Donald R. Schmitt was co-director of special investigations at the J. Allen Hynek Center for UFO Studies and, with Kevin Randle, co-authored 'UFO Crash at Roswell' (1991) and 'The Truth About the UFO Crash at Roswell' (1994) - the pair of books that converted Roswell from a 1980 paperback claim into a subject Congress asked the General Accounting Office to audit. The two books advanced substantially different crash scenarios from each other, which is itself part of the record: the 1994 book relocated the impact site and revised the timeline relative to 1991, on the strength of witnesses who were later withdrawn. Schmitt subsequently partnered with Thomas J. Carey on 'Witness to Roswell' (2007) and 'Inside the Real Area 51' (2013), continuing to develop the deathbed-testimony strand of the case, most importantly the sealed 2002 affidavit of Walter Haut. Schmitt's credibility was damaged in the mid-1990s when it emerged that he had misrepresented his professional background to fellow researchers, and Randle broke with him publicly over it. This board records that because a witness-chain researcher's own reliability is load-bearing on every uncorroborated witness he introduces.
